title: Payment Service Timeout / Failure
steps: Check Grafana dashboard: payments-overview for error rate and p99 latency.
Verify the payments pod is healthy: kubectl get pods -n payments.
Check downstream dependency (Stripe API) status at status.stripe.com.
If pods are crash-looping, inspect logs: kubectl logs -n payments -l app=payments --tail=200.
If latency spike only, check connection pool saturation in the payments DB metrics.
Restart the deployment if needed: kubectl rollout restart deployment/payments -n payments.
Escalate to #payments-eng if error rate does not drop within 10 minutes of restart.

title: Authentication Service Outage
steps: Confirm scope of impact: check whether login, token refresh, or both are failing.
Inspect auth service logs: kubectl logs -n auth -l app=auth-service --tail=200.
Verify Redis session store is reachable: redis-cli -h redis.auth.svc ping.
Check if a recent config or certificate rotation caused the issue: git log --oneline -5 in the auth-config repo.
If Redis is down, failover to the replica: kubectl exec -n auth redis-0 -- redis-cli cluster failover.
Restart auth pods: kubectl rollout restart deployment/auth-service -n auth.
Escalate to #identity-team if login success rate stays below 99% after restart.

title: Primary Database Connection Exhaustion
steps: Check active connections: SELECT count(*) FROM pg_stat_activity;
Identify long-running queries: SELECT pid, now() - pg_stat_activity.query_start AS duration, query FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE state = 'active' ORDER BY duration DESC LIMIT 10;
Check if connection pooler (PgBouncer) is saturated: show pools; in PgBouncer admin console.
Kill long-running idle-in-transaction sessions if safe: SELECT pg_terminate_backend(pid) FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE state = 'idle in transaction' AND query_start < now() - interval '10 minutes';
If PgBouncer is the bottleneck, increase max_client_conn and reload: pgbouncer -R.
Check for recent schema migrations that may have acquired locks: SELECT * FROM pg_locks WHERE granted = false;
Escalate to #data-platform if connections remain exhausted after clearing idle sessions.

title: Notification Delivery Delays
steps: Check the notification queue depth in Kafka: kafka-consumer-groups.sh --describe --group notification-workers.
Verify notification worker pods are running: kubectl get pods -n notifications.
Inspect worker logs for errors or backpressure: kubectl logs -n notifications -l app=notification-worker --tail=200.
Check downstream email provider (SendGrid) status at status.sendgrid.com.
If queue is growing, scale up workers: kubectl scale deployment/notification-worker -n notifications --replicas=6.
If messages are stuck on a specific partition, check for poison messages and skip if necessary.
Escalate to #notifications-eng if delivery latency exceeds SLA (5 minutes) after scaling.
